Risk items are loosely typed, so wrong fields are not caught.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports the risk card parts
sections.what: Brings in the icons, the store, the AI helper, and the card and badge pieces.
sections.why: Likely reason: needed to read app data, ask the AI helper for risks and draw the card.

sections.name: DeadlineRiskWidget (part 1)
sections.title: Loads and lists deadline risks
sections.what: Asks the AI helper for deadline risks whenever assignments, hackathons or internships change. Shows each risk with a Resolve Risk button and a count badge. The button sends the user to the semester or career screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the risk list up to date as deadlines change. Reason for the screen choice depending on type is not stated.
sections.watch_out: A failed AI call is treated as no risks, so the user sees all clear even though the check did not run.

sections.name: DeadlineRiskWidget (part 2)
sections.title: Shows the all-clear message
sections.what: When the risk list is empty, shows a green check and a message saying submissions are on track.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms that nothing needs attention, instead of showing a blank card.
sections.watch_out: This message appears both for real empty results and for failed checks, so it does not prove deadlines are safe.

summary: A card that lists assignments and hackathons at risk of missing their deadlines, with a button to jump to the place where each can be fixed.
purpose: Warns the user early about deadlines that look at risk.
why: Likely reason: keeps deadline problems visible in one place so they are not missed. The code does not say why the check is done by the AI helper.
how: When the card loads, and whenever assignments, hackathons or internships change, it asks the AI helper for a list of risks and stores it. Each risk shows its title, type and reason, with a Resolve Risk button. That button switches to the semester screen for assignments and to the career screen for other types. A count badge shows how many risks exist, and an all-clear message appears when there are none.
inputs: Assignments, hackathons and internships from the store. A list of risks from the predictDeadlineRisks function in the AI helper, where each risk should have an id, title, type and reason.
outputs: A count badge, a list of risk rows with buttons, or an all-clear message. Clicking a button changes the active tab in the store.
risks: If the AI helper fails, the card shows the same all-clear message as a real empty result, which can hide a problem. Each risk needs a unique id or the list may display incorrectly. The check reruns whenever those store lists change, which may happen often.
debug: If the card always says all clear, check predictDeadlineRisks in the aiAssistantEngine file and temporarily log errors instead of hiding them. If buttons send the user to the wrong screen, check the type values the AI helper returns. If the check runs too often, check how the store updates those lists.
